paragraphs: Riverton will convert four miles of downtown parking lanes into protected bike lanes by next summer, the city council decided on Tuesday. The 7-2 vote ends a debate that lasted almost two years. Construction is expected to begin in March.

Supporters pointed to the city's own crash data during the meeting. Since 2021, the three streets in the plan have accounted for 41 percent of all cyclist injuries in Riverton, even though they make up less than 5 percent of its road network. A pilot lane on Mill Street cut injuries there by half in its first year.

Not everyone is convinced. Several downtown shop owners argued that losing 300 parking spaces will drive customers to suburban malls. The council has promised to review sales data from the affected blocks after twelve months.
